modules.title: Introduction to Independence and the First Republic
modules.html:
Independence in 1960, the 1963 republic, political parties and the crises of the First Republic. This section covers introduction to independence and the first republic.

Key points

  • Nigeria became a Republic in the year _____. — 1963.
  • The first African country to gain independence from colonial rule in sub-Saharan Africa was _____. — Ghana.
  • Nigeria gained independence on: — Oct 1, 1960.
  • Nigeria gained independence in: — 1960.
  • Nigeria gained independence from Britain on... — October 1, 1960.

Worked examples

Q: Nigeria became a Republic in the year _____.
A: 1963 — While independence was gained in 1960, Nigeria became a Federal Republic in 1963, replacing the Queen as Head of State with a President.

Q: The first African country to gain independence from colonial rule in sub-Saharan Africa was _____.
A: Ghana — Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana became independent from Britain in 1957.

quiz.q: Nigeria became a Republic in the year _____.
quiz.solution: While independence was gained in 1960, Nigeria became a Federal Republic in 1963, replacing the Queen as Head of State with a President.

quiz.q: The first African country to gain independence from colonial rule in sub-Saharan Africa was _____.
quiz.solution: Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana became independent from Britain in 1957.

quiz.q: Nigeria gained independence on:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Oct 1, 1960.

quiz.q: Nigeria gained independence in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1960.

quiz.q: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: October 1, 1960.

quiz.q: The Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 was significant because it _____.
options: formally partitioned Africa among European powers
quiz.solution: The Berlin Conference, hosted by Bismarck, established the 'effective occupation' principle for the European scramble and partition of Africa.

quiz.q: King Jaja of Opobo was exiled to the West Indies in 1887 because he _____.
options: interfered with British trade in the hinterland
quiz.solution: Jaja was a threat to British economic interests in the Niger Delta as he insisted on his right to trade directly with European firms without middlemen.

quiz.q: The Sagrenti War of 1874 was fought between the British and the _____.
quiz.solution: The Sagrenti War (named after Garnet Wolseley) was one of the Anglo-Asante wars in present-day Ghana, resulting in the burning of Kumasi.

quiz.q: The Fulani Empire was divided into two administrative sectors with headquarters at _____.
quiz.solution: Usman dan Fodio divided the administration between his son Mohammed Bello (Sokoto) and his brother Abdullahi (Gwandu).

quiz.q: The kingdom of Dahomey was known for its unique military unit of _____.
quiz.solution: Dahomey’s 'Mino' (our mothers) were an elite female military regiment that played a major role in its 18th and 19th-century wars.

quiz.q: The 'Dahomey Gap' is a geographical feature that influenced _____.
options: the isolation of the forest kingdoms
the ease of movement for savannah armies
quiz.solution: The gap in the West African forest allowed savannah states like Oyo to use cavalry closer to the coast than in other regions.

quiz.q: The 1851 bombardment of Lagos was carried out to remove Oba _____.
quiz.solution: Oba Kosoko was ousted by the British because he supported the slave trade; he was replaced by Akintoye.

quiz.q: The legendary founder of Ile-Ife and the Yoruba race is _____.
quiz.solution: Oduduwa is regarded in Yoruba mythology as the progenitor of the Yoruba people and their kings.

quiz.q: The Nok Culture is famous for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Terracotta heads.

quiz.q: The 'Warrant Chief' system was unpopular in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Eastern Nigeria.

quiz.q: The motion for self-government in 1953 was moved by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Anthony Enahoro.

quiz.q: Apartheid policy was practiced in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: South Africa.

quiz.q: Herbert Macaulay is called the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Father of Nigerian Nationalism.

quiz.q: Queen Amina was a legendary warrior of:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Zaria.

quiz.q: Badagry was famous for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Slave trade.

quiz.q: The Bombardment of Lagos occurred in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: 1851.

quiz.q: The first Prime Minister was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Tafawa Balewa.

quiz.q: Nana of Itsekiri resisted:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: British.

quiz.q: June 12 1993 winner:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: MKO Abiola.

quiz.q: Herbert Macaulay founded:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: NNDP.

quiz.q: Currency change to Naira:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1973.

quiz.q: The NPC (Northern People's Congress) was led by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Sir Ahmadu Bello.

quiz.q: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern protectorates took place in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: 1914.

quiz.q: The Ogboni society was a feature of:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Yoruba politics.

quiz.q: The June 12, 1993 election was won by:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: M.K.O. Abiola.
